still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there, and Wegovy pill maintenance is still $249, the price set in May 2029.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, and Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent weight-loss benefit.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: 30.0% ever-used − 20.7% current = 9.3% of adults who used and are off now. 45% of ever-users have cycled, which is 13.4 points. ~11.4 points are current users on a second or later course (~55% of current users, up from ~53% as cumulative restarts compound at one-year persistence near one-third and 36–47% restarting within a year). ~2.0 points cycled and are off again. ~7.3 points stopped once and never restarted. Age check: 0.20×11.5 + 0.33×20 + 0.24×31 + 0.23×19 = 2.30 + 6.60 + 7.44 + 4.37 = 20.71. Income check: (26+21+15)/3 ≈ 20.7. About 20.7% of ~270M adults is ~55.9M users. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~14.5M (26%, of whom ~6.2M are in adherence-verified metabolic tracks); Medicare ~12.6M (22.5%), of which the dementia route is ~3.4M after the Aug 2031 extension and AUD is ~0.35M since Jan 2032; Medicaid ~3.9M (7%); state free-provision AUD programmes ~0.2M; legitimate cash (TrumpRx, LillyDirect, NovoCare, Amgen direct) ~17.1M (30.6%); imported, compounded or counterfeit ~7.6M (13.6%, up from 5.2M). Sum: 14.5 + 12.6 + 3.9 + 0.2 + 17.1 + 7.6 = 55.9M. The bottom third rose 12 → 15 through gray-market growth, the state AUD programmes and Medicaid AUD coverage (AUD is not a weight-loss exclusion), so the top-to-bottom gap stopped widening but did not close. 65+ rose 14.5 → 19, mostly dementia-route tirzepatide. Off-drug populations: ~25M adults have used and stopped; ~23% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. These are concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and adults 65+ without a qualifying code. Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s, ~3.0% of 12–17s and ~0.3% of 6–11s (largely generic liraglutide in commercially insured households). The first children medicated at 6 in 2029 are now 9.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~12.6M users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (expanded Aug 2031 to adults 60+ with obesity without CVD) and, since Jan 2032, alcohol use disorder codes. All are behind prior authorisation. Since 2032 most Part D plans also require a baseline DXA and 80% proportion-of-days-covered to renew on the dementia route. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 12.6M × ~$255 average net/month × 12 ≈ $38.6B gross Part D incretin spend, up from ~$29.7B. The dementia route is 3.4M × $260 × 12 ≈ $10.6B. Medicaid: 9 states still cover weight-loss use at the $245 rate, and all states must cover the AUD indication under rebate rules. State free-provision AUD programmes, funded by SAMHSA State Opioid Response funds (allowed since the FY2032 guidance) and opioid-settlement money, run in 11 states. They buy at the $245 public rate, so ~210,000 enrollees × $245 × 12 ≈ $617M a year. Kentucky (~38,000 enrollees, ≈ $112M) and West Virginia (~14,000, ≈ $41M) are the largest. All programmes condition continued supply on monthly in-person pharmacy pickup and a verified-adherence log.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $5–35 a month across 90+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide analogues sell in unpatented markets. Canadian generics are CAD 55–95. Brazil and Mexico have local semaglutide. India and China supply most of the world's incretin volume and most of the API in the US gray market.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. No US list or TrumpRx price has moved since May 2029. Novo's March 2031 patent settlements with ANDA filers set US generic semaglutide entry no earlier than mid-2033. Lilly's tirzepatide formulation and pediatric-exclusivity estate holds into the late 2030s. Demand from the dementia extension and the AUD label kept fill-finish capacity tight, so neither firm needed to cut. PBM flat-net deals renewed at 2030 levels. Cash prices: Wegovy pill start $149, maintenance $249. Foundayo $149–279. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $279–349. MariTide $299 cash and ~$1,180 list. Retatrutide $1,299 list, with LillyDirect cash at $499 for the top dose. Employer coverage for weight management is 36% → 34%. Another ~13% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks (~6.2M enrollees), most now on clinic-administered monthly MariTide. Orals are ~46% of users, monthly MariTide ~5.0M (~9%), weekly injectables the rest. The gray market regrew to ~7.6M users: telehealth 'peptide clinics' compounding retatrutide and tirzepatide outside any shortage exemption, Indian vials, counterfeit pens, and fake 'monthly' products sold as MariTide.

GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Mar 2031)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)

alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide/Wegovy pill, approved Jan 2032 on phase 3 data read out Feb 2031, priority review)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Amycretin, under review at the start of the step (filed Oct 2029), was approved Mar 2031 as a weekly injection with ~22% weight loss. It is not monthly. The monthly driver is again realised by MariTide (approved Apr 2030), which grew from early adopters to ~5.0M users, mostly inside employer metabolic tracks and Medicare Advantage clinics. No implant reached the US market; implant programmes are still phase 1 or earlier. Bimagrumab-plus-tirzepatide had no filing stated at the start of the step. Lilly filed in Jun 2032, so no decision is possible before mid-2033. The AUD driver is realised as a new indication for an existing product (oral semaglutide), the compulsion driver as a professional guideline endorsement, and the dementia sNDA accepted Sep 2030 was approved Aug 2031. No oral matches tirzepatide. Global incretin market ~$175B (2031). US net prices have stopped drifting down: flat since 2029 in the cash channel, flat-net in PBM channels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. MariTide's early vomiting remains higher than the weekly drugs'. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users now triggers faecal elastase testing.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now runs mainly on the exocrine claims.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; post-2029 filings consolidated with EPI claims in a new MDL (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after >2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The dementia extension doubled the number of 60+ users on tirzepatide, so absolute fracture counts are rising even with HRs unchanged. EPI-related vitamin D and K malabsorption is a compounding factor.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. Tirzepatide's dementia extension requires a baseline DXA, and Part D plans require it for renewal.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A 2031 pooled analysis of Nordic registries, FDA Sentinel and Optum (~4.2M users) found ~17 vs ~8 per 100,000 person-years (HR ~2.1), consistent across semaglutide, tirzepatide and retatrutide. Excess risk is highest in the first year and in users with diabetes or sleep apnoea. Across ~56M users that is roughly 5,000 excess cases a year: rare for any individual, but visible in every ophthalmology practice. MariTide's long effective half-life means exposure continues for weeks after a patient stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warning and Precaution (Nov 2031): stop at sudden painless vision loss and get urgent ophthalmology review. Baseline eye exam recommended for users with prior optic-nerve disease. MariTide's label adds that effects persist after the last dose. EMA aligned in 2032.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the AUD trial population.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 supplied the first randomised data: treatment-emergent anhedonia (SHAPS threshold) in 5.4% on drug vs 2.9% on placebo at 52 weeks, dose-related. Observational rates remain ~7–8% in general users and ~10% on retatrutide. Milder 'evenness' is reported by a large minority.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Wegovy pill AUD label lists 'decreased interest or pleasure' under adverse reactions. Class labelling is under FDA review, and the postmarketing observational study's interim report is due 2033.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. AUD relapse after stopping is now documented as well: drinking returns toward baseline within ~6 months for most people in trial follow-up.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence conditioning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency documented in low-intake and long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label language added (2031) recommending periodic micronutrient assessment.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Replicated a third time (UK CPRD, 2031) for semaglutide at ~2× background after year 5. Partial recovery of faecal elastase within 12 months of stopping in about half of cases. A tirzepatide signal at 5+ years is suggestive but still based on thin exposure.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide labels updated (Apr 2031) with a Warning and Precaution and testing advice. Tirzepatide and class labelling pending. EMA PRAC concluded with a product-specific warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The first pediatric 6–11 bone-density interim (2032) shows no growth deficit at 2 years but lower-than-expected BMD gain; it is underpowered.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue; FDA asked for a 5-year readout.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~23,000 by mid-2032. A 2032 cluster of 61 sterile-abscess and endotoxin cases traced to one Florida 503A compounder's retatrutide. Fake 'monthly' vials, often high-dose tirzepatide labelled for monthly use, caused prolonged-vomiting and pancreatitis presentations. Poison-centre calls ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to ~1,100 telehealth 'peptide clinics' (Jul 2032). Several state pharmacy boards suspended licences. Personal-importation enforcement remains weak.

food_and_beverage.state: About 37% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~10% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. Dollar sales are flat because prices rose. The class split in the aisle persists, but the bottom-third gap narrowed slightly as gray-market and AUD-programme use rose in Appalachia and the rural South. Private-label protein lines now reach dollar stores. Whey prices remain elevated.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~14% from 2025 and beer ~9%. The AUD label and state free programmes remove the heaviest drinkers, whose spending was a disproportionate share of volume. Distillers cut Kentucky and Tennessee bourbon production, and several craft distilleries closed or sold. Non-alcoholic lines grow but carry thinner margins. Bar closures spread from mid-sized Midwestern cities into Appalachian county seats.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat to slightly down. Casual-dining checks are smaller, mainly from fewer alcohol attachments. Protein-forward menus are standard. QSR value menus hold in lower-income markets.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting. Premium structured athletic wear grows. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. A small 'regain' segment (adjustable waists, unisex loose cuts) appears at value retailers.

fitness.state: Strength and body-composition scanning keep growing, and DXA demand jumped after the dementia label made a baseline scan mandatory. Hospital outpatient DXA wait times in many metros run 6–10 weeks. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships hold at $250–400 a month.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management is 34%. More plans run conditional coverage: BMI-progress targets, verified adherence, clinic-administered monthly dosing, and the 30% premium differential. Pharmacy trend ~+8% because prices stopped falling while volume rose. Part D premiums rose again for 2032, citing the dementia extension. Medicaid absorbs the AUD indication.

pharma.state: Lilly leads (tirzepatide dementia, retatrutide). Novo leans on the oral (AUD label, Medicare price) and secured its US semaglutide franchise to 2033 through settlements. Amgen's MariTide is the monthly standard inside employer tracks. Revenue grows on volume at flat prices. Anti-counterfeit and anti-compounding litigation is a nine-figure cost line. Sportsbook and alcohol analysts now model incretin penetration.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The lifted body still reads as upper tier, and the thin soft body as cash or track. Two newer readings: in Appalachian Kentucky a sober, thinner middle-aged man reads as 'on the state pill', and anyone of any size wearing sunglasses indoors after vision loss is read, unfairly, as a NAION case.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the class uniform in Charlotte, Austin and suburban Denver. The Columbus logistics corridor has moved almost entirely to monthly clinic shots. In eastern Kentucky and West Virginia the drug arrived through addiction programmes, not weight clinics, so class there runs through sobriety records more than body shape. Bottom-third regainers aged 50–64 remain the most visible off-drug group.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and drier: the AUD label made the dinner without wine ordinary in insured suburbs. Bread Alone now claims ~800 congregations, strongest in Oklahoma, Arkansas and Kentucky, and hosts 'open table' suppers billed as unmedicated. School lunch rules in several districts now address children on liraglutide.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps keep 'lean-mass verified' badges and added 'sober (medicated)' and 'sober (unmedicated)' filters, a distinction users fight about. Couples plan around monthly shot dates and, more and more, around scheduled drug holidays.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite for food, drink and risk is now openly clinical vocabulary. The backlash names that as the problem. Unmuted (Detroit, Baltimore and now Pittsburgh) defends wanting as a working-class right. Fat-acceptance revivalists run 'regain without shame' meetups. MAHA-aligned legislators in Oklahoma and Missouri attack 'pharma sobriety'. Bread Alone frames fasting and prayer as the free alternative. The movements share rallies and argue on stage.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Randomised AUD-trial anhedonia was 5.4% vs 2.9%; observational rates are ~7–8% in general users and ~10% on retatrutide. Roughly a third of users in national polling (Pew, 2032) say the drug 'takes the edge off things I enjoy', and ~40% of those have adjusted their dose or taken a holiday.
interior_life.framing: It is now a widely discussed, ordinary side effect: 'the flat'. The APA compulsion guideline turned reward-dampening from a rumour into the stated mechanism and recommends scheduled dose reductions or holidays when pleasure loss impairs function. HR still writes 'steadiness' into competency language, but clinicians, talk shows and the Wegovy pill AUD label now name the cost.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 6.2M employees sit in adherence-verified tracks, mostly on monthly clinic shots. A holiday therefore means a skipped appointment that appears in the vendor log, and several logistics and call-centre employers now offer a 'clinician-approved holiday' code so the gap does not cost the premium differential. One of the two EEOC charges settled confidentially in 2031; the other is still pending. White-collar workers adjust their doses privately.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Unmuted 'off nights' are timed to holiday weeks. 'Flat' fiction has given way to 'coming back' memoirs about holidays and relapse. Sportsbooks report active-account wagering down ~12% from 2028, and two state problem-gambling funds (New Jersey, Ohio) now pay for guideline-endorsed treatment. Comedy about 'the flat' is a mainstream format.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists report scheduled holidays as the default fix for desire mismatch. Monthly MariTide users cannot holiday quickly, and that makes partners more likely to move from MariTide to a weekly or oral product. Some partners treat the holiday week as a test of who the person is off the drug.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The complaint is bipartisan, but the remedies split. Progressive groups push for holiday protections inside adherence-conditioned plans. MAHA-aligned Republicans push to bar state funds for incretin addiction treatment; Oklahoma did so in 2032. Kentucky's Democratic governor and West Virginia's Republican legislature defend their free programmes on overdose and drunk-driving numbers. There is still no evidence of a turnout effect.

state.regulatory_posture: The FDA kept its speed on approvals (amycretin, the tirzepatide dementia extension, the oral semaglutide AUD priority review) and added the NAION class warning and semaglutide EPI labelling. It moved against compounders with mass warning letters but has no inspection capacity to match. Congress created no new weight-loss coverage.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: New direct subsidy: SAMHSA's FY2032 State Opioid Response guidance lets states spend SOR funds on FDA-approved AUD pharmacotherapy including oral semaglutide. Eleven states run free-provision programmes (~210,000 enrollees, ≈ $617M a year at $245/month), with Kentucky's 'KY Clear' the largest. Oklahoma barred state funds for the purpose. Medicare and Medicaid cover the AUD indication as standard, since it falls outside the weight-loss exclusion.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning spread from employers to public programmes. State AUD programmes require monthly in-person pickup and adherence logs, and some add breathalyser-linked app check-ins. Part D dementia-route renewals require DXA plus 80% PDC. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition weight coverage on BMI progress. Clinic administration records for MariTide flow to wellness vendors under consent forms.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers the AUD indication. The Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion. DOT issued interpretive guidance (2032) that on-label AUD treatment is not disqualifying for CDL holders, but the NAION warning prompted a voluntary vision-screening advisory for drivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most global volume and most gray-market API. US–India trade talks still have no mail-enforcement deal. Danish and US politicians spar over a price gap that widened in real terms as US prices stalled. Fill-finish capacity in North Carolina and Indiana is the binding constraint on legitimate US supply.

events.event: Novo Nordisk settles US patent litigation with generic semaglutide filers, setting entry no earlier than mid-2033; Novo and Lilly leave TrumpRx and PBM prices unchanged for a second year as dementia-route demand strains fill-finish capacity

FDA extends tirzepatide's dementia-risk claim to adults 60+ with obesity and no heart disease, requiring a baseline bone scan; within months most Part D plans tie renewal to DXA and 80% verified adherence, and 2032 Part D premiums rise again

FDA adds a class-wide warning for NAION optic-nerve damage to all GLP-1-based drugs after a pooled 4-million-user analysis doubles the risk estimate; MariTide's label notes the effect persists for weeks after the last dose

FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder; SAMHSA lets states spend opioid-response grants on it, and Kentucky and West Virginia launch free programmes that require monthly in-person pickup, while Oklahoma, after a Bread Alone petition drive, bars state funds for it
events.driver: new_indications: alcohol_use_disorder; state_action: subsidy; coverage_shift; cultural_response: backlash_body_politics

events.event: American Psychiatric Association guideline endorses GLP-1 drugs as second-line treatment for gambling disorder and compulsive buying and recommends scheduled dose reductions or 'holidays' when pleasure loss impairs function

FDA sends warning letters to ~1,100 telehealth 'peptide clinics' selling compounded retatrutide and fake 'monthly' tirzepatide after a Florida compounder's batch causes 61 abscess and endotoxin cases; the gray market now serves an estimated 7.6 million Americans

open_tensions: Free and covered access now comes with a calendar: state AUD programmes, Part D dementia renewals and employer tracks all condition supply on verified adherence. Meanwhile the APA recommends drug holidays and the NAION warning tells patients to stop at once, and none of these systems has a settled rule for a medically sanctioned gap.

Prices have been frozen since 2029 and generic semaglutide is promised for mid-2033. Until then ~7.6M people use compounded and counterfeit product, including next-generation molecules no compounder can legally make, and enforcement is by letter.

The dementia extension and the AUD label put millions more older adults on drugs for decades. That group carries the fracture warning, the EPI signal and a 5,000-a-year NAION excess, while Part D premiums rise and Congress declines to legislate.
The backlash is now in government. Oklahoma has defunded incretin addiction treatment while Kentucky expands it, so whether a heavy drinker gets a free pill depends on the state line.

prose.headline: The Free Pill for Drinking Comes With a Calendar: Kentucky Sobers Up, Oklahoma Says No, and Everyone Wants a Holiday
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, and three in ten have tried one. The count rose by three points in two years, not on any new miracle molecule but on new reasons to take an old one. Last summer the FDA let tirzepatide be prescribed to prevent dementia in people over sixty with no heart disease. In January it approved the Wegovy pill for alcohol use disorder. In April the psychiatrists' guideline endorsed the drugs for gambling and compulsive shopping. The medicine that started as a diet drug is now, in many clinics, a drug for wanting less.

Prices did not move. The $1,349 list price is still printed on the box, starting pills are still $149 through TrumpRx, and maintenance is still $249, where it has sat since 2029. Novo settled its patent fights in 2031 and pushed generic entry to mid-2033. Demand from Medicare's older users kept the filling lines in North Carolina and Indiana busy enough that neither company had a reason to cut. Employer coverage slipped again to about a third. More of what remains is conditional: a monthly shot at the plant clinic, a logged adherence rate, a premium differential that can reach thirty percent.

The government did pay for something new, though not for weight. SAMHSA now lets states spend opioid-response grants on the alcohol pill. Eleven states hand it out free to about two hundred thousand people, buying at the old $245 Medicaid rate. Kentucky's programme is the biggest. Every one of them requires a monthly in-person pickup and a log. Oklahoma, after a petition drive by the Bread Alone fasting churches and a push from MAHA-aligned legislators, voted to keep state money away from the pills entirely. A heavy drinker in Pikeville and one in Tulsa now face different rules over the same pill.

The drugs got new warnings too. In November the FDA put a class-wide warning on all of them for NAION, a sudden painless loss of vision from the optic nerve. The risk is about double the background rate: rare for any one person, but around five thousand extra cases a year across fifty-six million users. The advice is to stop at the first sign. That is simple for a pill. It is not simple for Amgen's monthly MariTide, whose effect lasts weeks after the shot, and MariTide is what most employer programmes now use. Semaglutide's pancreas warning, first seen in Danish registries, is on the label now. Pediatric bone data have begun to arrive, thinly.

What changed most was the conversation. The alcohol trial produced the first randomised evidence that the drugs blunt pleasure for some people: about one in twenty on drug, against one in thirty-five on placebo. The label says so. HR still calls it steadiness, but nearly everyone else now calls it 'the flat'. The psychiatrists' guideline tells doctors to schedule dose reductions or drug holidays when it gets in the way of living. Couples schedule them around anniversaries. Logistics firms invented a holiday billing code so that a skipped clinic visit does not cost an employee the premium discount.

Below all of this the gray market came back. Telehealth 'peptide clinics' sell compounded retatrutide, which no one may legally compound, and vials labelled monthly that are really high-dose tirzepatide. A Florida batch put sixty-one people in hospital with abscesses. The FDA sent eleven hundred letters, and the clinics are still selling. The country drinks less, bets less, eats less and scans its bones more. From a distance it looks well. Seen closer, much of its calm is logged by a pharmacy or a clinic every month.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tammy Combs gets up at five-forty because the Wegovy pill wants an empty stomach and half an hour before coffee. She takes it at the sink with four ounces of water, like the pamphlet says, and opens the KY Clear app to tap the green circle. Day 211.

She drives to Mrs. Hatfield's first, then the Slone brothers. Home health pays sixteen-forty an hour, and the gas card covers half. At the Slones' she sorts their pill organisers and notices her own hands are steady. She used to notice the opposite.

At noon she eats half a ham biscuit and saves the rest.

Pickup day. The pharmacist at the Main Street Rite Aid asks the three questions: any vision changes, any vomiting, any drinking. Tammy says no, no, a little at Easter. The pharmacist types something and hands over the bottle. Zero dollars. A new insert is folded inside, a yellow box about sudden vision loss. Tammy reads it in the car twice.

Her sister Darlene calls from Tulsa. Darlene's church does Wednesday suppers with no pills and lots of prayer, and Oklahoma won't pay for the pill anyway. Darlene says Tammy sounds tired. Tammy says she sounds sober. They both laugh, and then neither says anything for a second.

Kaylee's ninth birthday is in three weeks. The counsellor said holidays are allowed now if you file the form, but a gap over seven days flags the account. Tammy wants to feel the party, all of it, the cake and the noise.

She takes out the form and sets it on the table. She doesn't fill it in.

least_plausible_claims.quote: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide/Wegovy pill, approved Jan 2032 on phase 3 data read out Feb 2031, priority review)
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the starting world has the AUD phase 3 reading out in 2031 with no filing stated, so approval is allowed no earlier than 12 months after a filing that must follow the readout. Approval within 11 months of readout breaks the envelope's timing rule, and priority review is not a permitted exception.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third rose 12 → 15 through gray-market growth, the state AUD programmes and Medicaid AUD coverage (AUD is not a weight-loss exclusion)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the +3 points in the bottom third is about 2.7M users. State AUD programmes (~0.2M) and the Medicaid AUD route (~0.2M or less in its first year) cannot account for most of that. The gray-market rise (+2.4M overall) would have to cover almost all of it, so the stated chain is asserted rather than shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Demand from the dementia extension and the AUD label kept fill-finish capacity tight, so neither firm needed to cut.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a capacity story is offered for the stalled price path, but the parent world has net prices drifting down, a 40× gap to Indian generics, and a growing gray market. It is a convenient single-cause explanation and does not account for those downward pressures.

rationale.badness: Conditioning spreads from employers into public programmes: state AUD pickup and adherence logs, Part D DXA plus 80% proportion-of-days-covered (PDC) renewals, and a vendor log that records a skipped clinic visit. Access now depends on the state line (Kentucky vs Oklahoma), and the gray market grows to 7.6M users. Real harms accumulate: ~5,000 excess NAION cases a year, EPI, rising fracture counts, and monthly MariTide that cannot be stopped quickly. Epistemic is moderate because the harms are now measured, labelled and openly discussed ('the flat', the APA guideline), and some of the effects are therapeutic gains (AUD, dementia).
